result:
The proposed answer of 186 is off by one; I believe the correct minimum is 185. I reasoned this through and did not verify the lower bound rigorously.

**Setup.** Ana's data is ambiguous between primes p and q exactly when some nonconstant p-periodic f and some nonconstant q-periodic g agree on the chosen set S. Suppose S covers every residue mod p and mod q. If the graph on S with edges x~y whenever x≡y mod p or mod q is connected, then any such pair of functions would be constant on S. That contradicts f being nonconstant, so Ana can distinguish p from q.

**Upper bound.** For S = {0,…,n−1}, the graph with steps p and q is connected exactly when n ≥ p+q−gcd(p,q) = p+q−1. The hardest pair is 97 and 89, which needs n ≥ 185. With n = 185, every pair of primes below 100 gives a connected graph, and S covers all residues mod each prime. So 185 integers suffice.

**Lower bound.** I recall this problem's known answer as 97+89−1 = 185. The proposed solution's own argument also uses connectivity, which gives p+q−1 rather than p+q.

The proposed answer of 186 therefore overcounts by one.

VERDICT: REJECT
